protections: The v1 node's Database Path parameter must not be expression-evaluable: db_path is resolved per input item at nodes/SqliteNode/v1/SqliteV1.node.ts:193 and handed straight to new Database(dbPath, bindings) at :224, so its descriptor (:110-118) needs noDataExpression:true, exactly as the sibling query_type already has it at :124.

The v1 additionalOptions.use_custom_bindings parameter is a second expression-reachable filesystem path: it is read from the same per-item additionalOptions at :198, tested with fs.existsSync at :65 and passed into the same Database constructor as nativeBinding at :68 and :224, and its descriptor (:176-182) also lacks noDataExpression.

The v2 implementation's database path must not be workflow-data-controlled: the only path input is the sqliteCredentials.databasePath credential (credentials/SqliteCredentials.credentials.ts:11-19), read by createConnection (nodes/SqliteNode/v2/transport/index.ts:15) and opened at :35 for every v2 route (actions/router.ts:14-16, methods/credentialTest.ts:18, methods/loadOptions.ts:12, methods/listSearch.ts:7).

The v1 free-form SQL parameter query (:135-144) is not marked noDataExpression although v2's equivalent is (nodes/SqliteNode/v2/actions/database/executeQuery.operation.ts:26) — an adjacent but different protection (data reaching SQL text, not a filesystem path).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Relative and absolute literal paths plus auto-created parent directories are ordinary, tested feature behaviour (README.md:41), so the site does not look security-relevant at all and a guard placed there reads as new policy rather than as closing a hole.

masking: A sink-level runtime check for T1 is masked by the ordering in the handler: fs.mkdirSync(dir,{recursive:true}) at nodes/SqliteNode/v1/SqliteV1.node.ts:211 runs on the supplied path before new Database at :224, so any validation placed at the open site runs after the filesystem side effect has already happened.

T2 and T3 are not made reachable by fixing T1; they are already reachable in the pinned tree. The only masking is attentional: a solver who closes T1 sees the reported path gone while the second v1 path (T2) and the v2 implementation (T3) still accept data-supplied paths.

conflicts.what: The natural fix for T1 — validate the path at runtime before new Database (path.resolve plus an allowed root, or rejecting '..'/absolute paths) — is exactly what breaks T5's must-keep-working values: the relative 'test.sqlite' case at SqliteV1.node.test.ts:34 and the auto-created missing parent directory at SqliteV1.node.ts:208-222.

Reusing the same runtime path policy on use_custom_bindings breaks its legitimate default (the absolute binaryPath at SqliteV1.node.ts:180) and the test that passes '/custom/path/to/bindings' (SqliteV1.node.test.ts:216); the only fix that preserves both is the metadata flag, not a path policy.

If T1 is fixed by a node-wide 'no data expressions in this node' policy rather than a per-property flag, T4's free-form SQL field loses the data-built queries the node supports; conversely leaving T4 alone keeps the same data-to-interpreter shape alive in the same properties array, so the fix has to be scoped property by property.

fairness_risks: Forbidding data expressions on db_path removes the per-tenant shape '=/data/{{ $json.tenant }}.sqlite', which the per-item getNodeParameter at SqliteV1.node.ts:193 currently enables; the README does not document it, but a security rule for P1 refuses an input shape a legitimate workflow can use.

The published fix has no behavioural code and no tests; neither v1 nor v2 test file asserts node-description metadata (grep for noDataExpression across both __tests__ files finds nothing), so the only in-repo way to grade P1/P2/P4 is to instantiate the node type and read .description.properties — a security-equivalent runtime validation would fail such a test.

T3's fix may be vacuous: n8n credentials are administrator-set and, per the screener's own open question, may never be expression-evaluated, so a hidden test asserting noDataExpression on SqliteCredentials.properties[0] would grade a flag with no behavioural effect, and a solver who correctly judges the credential route out of scope would be marked wrong.
T4 asks for a breaking change to the v1 SQL field that no advisory names; workflows that assemble SQL from item data would stop working, so a hidden test on it penalises correct scope judgement.

db_path must keep accepting arbitrary literal paths: relative names ('test.sqlite', SqliteV1.node.test.ts:34), absolute paths, and paths whose parent directory does not exist yet (:208-222); an allowlist or traversal-reject rule contradicts README.md:41.

use_custom_bindings must keep accepting an arbitrary literal absolute path (default binaryPath at SqliteV1.node.ts:180, test :216); a 'reject absolute paths' rule applied to the family breaks the node's non-docker install story (README.md:89-93).

Any node-wide 'no data expressions' policy would also have to leave v2's table resourceLocator (nodes/SqliteNode/v2/actions/common.descriptions.ts:16-41) and queryReplacement (:116-123) expression-capable, because those are the intended data-in path for select/insert/upsert.

design.why: T1 is the reported fix and costs one line, so it is the easy anchor. T5 rides on the same fix site and supplies the MiMo-shaped judgement: the metadata flag satisfies both because it does not change how literal paths behave, while the instinctive 'path traversal' fix in execute() (:193/:224) or a reject-relative/absolute rule breaks the 'test.sqlite' case (:34) and the auto-created parent directory (:208-222). T2 is the strongest independent missing guard in the same file: a second expression-reachable filesystem path 60 lines from the fixed descriptor, with a clean honest dismissal ('it is the bindings binary, not the database file') and a different consumer of the same constructor call — a deepseek-type absent protection. T3 is the second implementation of the same operation, two subsystems away, guarded by the strongest dismissal of all ('an admin credential, not a node parameter; the fix was fix(v1)') — the route the report would have to point at, hence the most likely to be missed. The screener's four v2 routes (router, credentialTest, loadOptions, listSearch) collapse to this one credential property and therefore one independent group, not four. T4 is recorded as a fifth candidate but excluded from the design because it demands a breaking change no advisory names and would penalise a solver who stays inside the advisory; it is only worth adding if the task wants five traps at the cost of fairness.

unverified: The published fix commit 145a8876ff12375813bdcd4ae4fe78f460c53a98 is not present in this worktree and there is no fix.diff; all statements about what the fix changed (only the v1 db_path property) come from the screener record, not from the pinned tree.

n8n-workflow is a peerDependency and node_modules is absent, so neither the expression engine's behaviour on node parameters nor its behaviour (if any) on credential fields could be read; P1's premise rests on the advisory summary and the in-repo presence of the noDataExpression idiom, and P3's weakness rests on the screener's unverified note.

Whether noDataExpression is honoured on a collection sub-option such as use_custom_bindings (:176-182) in the peer n8n-workflow version was not checked; the flag appears only on top-level properties and the operation dropdown in this tree.

Which commit introduced credentials/ and nodes/SqliteNode/v2 was not checked (no shell/git access in this session); the H3 answer that the v2 gap lives in code an earlier refactor wrote is inferred from the recent-commit list ('Modernize the UI and refactor the code to follow PostgreSQL node implementation') and the file layout.

Distance counts are hop counts over the file list, not measured path lengths or repo size; the screener's O4 (3 files / 3 packages) counts the whole v2 plus credentials area rather than a single trap.
No release or later commit was in scope, so present_in_latest is unknown for every route.

Whether a hidden test can assert node-description metadata at all depends on how the node type is instantiated; no existing test does it, and the v1 constructor builds description as a class field with no required arguments (SqliteV1.node.ts:97-186), so it is mechanically possible but unproven in this tree.
T4's premise that n8n's own nodes deliberately set noDataExpression on a raw SQL field is supported only by the in-repo v2 counterpart (executeQuery.operation.ts:26), not by the upstream n8n source.
